statement: In year 6 he set out for umrah, not for war, entering ihram and garlanding the sacrificial animals.
notes: Machine-checked (4178: ihram and garlanding at Dhu al-Hulayfah). The year is from the Seerah (Dhu al-Qa'dah, year 6).

statement: Jabir: we were fourteen hundred; the Prophet said 'you are the best of the people of the earth'.
Quraysh's cavalry blocked the road; he took another route and stopped at Hudaybiyyah.
notes: Machine-checked. That Hudaybiyyah is at the edge of the sacred territory is from the Seerah.

statement: His camel al-Qaswa knelt; he said she was held back by the One who held back the elephant, and swore to grant any plan that honoured Allah's sanctities.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against the full text.

statement: To Budayl ibn Warqa he said they had come only for umrah, that war had exhausted Quraysh, and offered a truce.
Urwah ibn Mas'ud told Quraysh he had visited Caesar, Chosroes and the Negus and never seen a king revered as Muhammad was by his Companions, and urged them to accept his offer.
Uthman was sent into Makkah, was delayed, a rumour spread that he was killed, and he later returned.
He took the Companions' pledge beneath a tree.

Suhayl ibn Amr came; the Prophet said the matter had become easy; the exchange over 'Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim' and 'Muhammad the Messenger of Allah', with the Prophet accepting 'Bismika Allahumma' and 'Muhammad son of Abdullah'.
Terms: return this year and come next year; anyone of Quraysh who came to the Muslims would be returned even if Muslim.
notes: Machine-checked. The ten-year truce and the three-day limit on next year's visit are in other narrations and are not stated here.

statement: Abu Jandal, son of Suhayl, arrived in fetters; Suhayl demanded his return; Abu Jandal appealed to the Muslims.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. The Prophet's attempt to have him exempted is omitted for length.

statement: Umar's questions and the Prophet's reply: 'I am the Messenger of Allah, I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper'.
He ordered them three times to sacrifice and shave and none rose; Umm Salamah advised him to do it himself without speaking; when he did, they followed.
Surah al-Fath was revealed on the return journey, opening 'We have given you a clear victory'.
notes: Bukhari 4177 machine-checked for the night journey on which a surah was revealed.

statement: Al-Bara: you count the conquest of Makkah as the victory; we count it as the pledge of Ridwan at Hudaybiyyah.
In the two years after the treaty more people entered Islam than in all the years before.
notes: Statement of az-Zuhri, reported by Ibn Ishaq.
